item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "c30afb7f80c0ca9be9e9acb16a55472ffe917a07b801cd522acc174650161f12",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "A record of cell properties containing one value of type Parameter, as specified by its constructor D007 and projection D002.",
      "effect_on_target": "The existential witness assigns such a record to each cell. The final inequality compares entire records.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "The first projection of a cell-property record, returning its Parameter value.",
      "effect_on_target": "The first two conclusions constrain the assigned record's averagedParameter field.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "A structure consisting of a Parameter-valued operation on a model, measure, cell, and parameter field, together with locality and conditional constant-preservation laws specified by D008.",
      "effect_on_target": "Quantification over averagingRule includes both laws as bundled assumptions; the operation is not defined by an integral.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "LocalDef004",
      "meaning": "The first projection of an averaging-rule structure: an operation Model → Measure Point → Cell → (Point → Parameter) → Parameter.",
      "effect_on_target": "This operation supplies all cell averages in the hypotheses and conclusions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "LocalDef005",
      "meaning": "A grid structure containing a domain and cell regions, with a nonempty cell type, measurable regions, disjoint regions for distinct cells, and exact coverage of the domain, as specified by D009.",
      "effect_on_target": "The grid binder imposes these partition properties on the regions used for locality and measure restrictions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "LocalDef006",
      "meaning": "The second projection of a grid, assigning to each cell a subset of Point.",
      "effect_on_target": "These subsets determine which region is measured and where parameter fields must agree.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "LocalDef007",
      "meaning": "Constructs a cell-property record from a single Parameter value.",
      "effect_on_target": "An average can be packaged as a cell-property record without supplying any further data or conditions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "LocalDef008",
      "meaning": "Constructs an averaging rule from an operation A and two laws: for every model, measure, cell, and pair of fields agreeing pointwise on that cell's region, their A-values are equal; for every model, measure, cell, and parameter p, if the region's measure is neither zero nor infinity, then A applied to the globally constant field p equals p.",
      "effect_on_target": "Locality is assumed for all measures and fields. Constant preservation is assumed on cells of positive finite measure. These bundled laws support the second and third conclusions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "LocalDef009",
      "meaning": "Constructs a grid from a domain Ω, a family R of cell regions, a proof that Cell is nonempty, measurability of every R(c), disjointness of R(c₁) and R(c₂) whenever c₁ ≠ c₂, and the equivalence x ∈ Ω if and only if there exists c with x ∈ R(c).",
      "effect_on_target": "The regions form an exactly disjoint measurable partition of the stored domain. No finiteness, countability, geometry, or coverage of all Point is required.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction.",
      "effect_on_target": "All four conclusions must hold for the same assigned-cell-properties function.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "DFunLike.coe",
      "meaning": "Extracts the function represented by a function-like object.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows the measure to be evaluated on a cell region.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "ENNReal",
      "meaning": "The extended nonnegative real numbers, obtained by adjoining a top element infinity to the nonnegative reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Cell measures take values in [0, ∞]; excluding zero and infinity means positive finite measure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two elements of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The conclusions assert exact equality of Parameter values, not approximation or equality almost everywhere.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "Exists",
      "meaning": "Existential quantification over a specified type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The hypothesis supplies two cells with unequal averages; the conclusion supplies one assignment and two cells with unequal assigned records.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "MeasurableSpace",
      "meaning": "A measurable-space structure specifying a sigma-algebra on a type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Point carries a measurable structure used by the measure and the measurability requirements on cell regions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "MeasureTheory.Measure",
      "meaning": "A measure on the supplied measurable space, with values in the extended nonnegative reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "volumeMeasure is an arbitrary measure on Point; its name does not impose a geometric volume interpretation.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike",
      "meaning": "Represents a measure as a function from sets to extended nonnegative reals by evaluating its underlying outer measure.",
      "effect_on_target": "The expressions volumeMeasure(R(c)) are set-measure evaluations. Grid regions are additionally known to be measurable.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D018",
      "name": "Ne",
      "meaning": "Inequality, defined as the negation of equality.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses exclusion of zero and infinity for cell measures and exact inequality of averages and assigned records.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D019",
      "name": "OfNat.ofNat",
      "meaning": "Extracts the interpretation of a natural-number literal from its type's numeral instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the literal 0 in the cell-measure hypothesis as zero in ENNReal.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D020",
      "name": "Set",
      "meaning": "A set of elements of a type is a predicate on that type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The domain and cell regions are subsets of Point without any additional geometric structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D021",
      "name": "Set.EqOn",
      "meaning": "Two functions agree on a set when their values are equal at every point belonging to that set.",
      "effect_on_target": "The second conclusion requires pointwise agreement throughout the selected cell region; it does not use almost-everywhere agreement.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D022",
      "name": "Top.top",
      "meaning": "Extracts the distinguished top element of a type with a Top instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Together with D024, denotes infinity in the finiteness hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D023",
      "name": "Zero.toOfNat0",
      "meaning": "Uses a type's zero element as its interpretation of the numeral 0.",
      "effect_on_target": "Connects the written zero in the measure hypothesis to the ENNReal zero instance.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D024",
      "name": "instTopENNReal",
      "meaning": "The top element of ENNReal is the adjoined top of WithTop, namely infinity.",
      "effect_on_target": "Each cell measure must differ from infinity.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D025",
      "name": "instZeroENNReal",
      "meaning": "The zero of ENNReal is the embedded zero of the nonnegative reals.",
      "effect_on_target": "Each cell measure must differ from zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D026",
      "name": "CompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra.toCompleteBooleanAlgebra",
      "meaning": "Projects the complete Boolean algebra structure from a complete atomic Boolean algebra.",
      "effect_on_target": "Participates in obtaining the ordinary set-order structure used to interpret disjointness of cell regions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D027",
      "name": "CompleteBooleanAlgebra.toCompleteDistribLattice",
      "meaning": "Builds the complete distributive lattice structure from a complete Boolean algebra, retaining its complete lattice and associated operations.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides inherited order infrastructure for sets; it introduces no additional restriction on the grid.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D028",
      "name": "CompleteBooleanAlgebra.toCompleteLattice",
      "meaning": "Projects the complete lattice underlying a complete Boolean algebra.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies part of the inherited set-order structure used in grid disjointness.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D029",
      "name": "CompleteDistribLattice.toFrame",
      "meaning": "Projects the frame structure underlying a complete distributive lattice.",
      "effect_on_target": "Participates in obtaining the bottom element and order structure on sets used in disjointness.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D030",
      "name": "CompleteLattice.instOmegaCompletePartialOrder",
      "meaning": "Equips a complete lattice with an omega-complete partial order whose increasing-chain supremum is the indexed supremum of the chain.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides an inherited partial-order instance for sets; the proposition makes no separate assertion about chains or limits.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D031",
      "name": "Disjoint",
      "meaning": "Two elements of a partial order with bottom are disjoint if every common lower bound lies below bottom. For sets ordered by inclusion, this means their intersection is empty.",
      "effect_on_target": "Distinct cell indices have regions with no common point, rather than merely overlap of measure zero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D032",
      "name": "HeytingAlgebra.toOrderBot",
      "meaning": "Projects the order-with-bottom structure from a Heyting algebra.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the empty set as bottom in the set-disjointness condition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D033",
      "name": "Iff",
      "meaning": "Logical equivalence, requiring implication in both directions.",
      "effect_on_target": "The grid's domain consists exactly of the points in at least one cell region.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D034",
      "name": "MeasurableSet",
      "meaning": "Membership of a set in the sigma-algebra specified by the measurable-space instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Every cell region is measurable as a bundled grid requirement.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D035",
      "name": "Membership.mem",
      "meaning": "Extracts the membership relation of a membership instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets point membership in the grid's domain and cell regions, including the set on which fields agree.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D036",
      "name": "Nonempty",
      "meaning": "The proposition that a type has at least one element.",
      "effect_on_target": "A grid includes a proof that Cell is inhabited. The unequal-average hypothesis further forces at least two distinct cells.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D037",
      "name": "OmegaCompletePartialOrder.toPartialOrder",
      "meaning": "Projects the partial order underlying an omega-complete partial order.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides set inclusion as the order used in the disjointness definition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D038",
      "name": "Order.Frame.toHeytingAlgebra",
      "meaning": "Extracts a Heyting algebra from a frame using its lattice, top, implication, bottom, and complement structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides inherited set-order infrastructure, including bottom, for interpreting cell disjointness.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D039",
      "name": "Set.instCompleteAtomicBooleanAlgebra",
      "meaning": "Equips sets with their complete atomic Boolean algebra structure: inclusion order, unions, intersections, whole set, empty set, and complements.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that the order-theoretic disjointness condition on cell regions has its ordinary set-theoretic meaning.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D040",
      "name": "Set.instMembership",
      "meaning": "Uses set membership as the membership relation for predicate-valued sets.",
      "effect_on_target": "Membership in a region or domain means that its defining predicate holds at the point.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify over arbitrary types Model, Cell, Point, and Parameter, in potentially different universes.",
      "Equip Point with a measurable-space structure.",
      "Universally quantify over a grid with domain Ω ⊆ Point and cell-region function R : Cell → Set Point, subject to its bundled partition conditions.",
      "Universally quantify over a measure μ on Point and an averaging-rule structure for Model, Cell, Point, Parameter, and this particular region function R.",
      "Universally quantify over a model m ∈ Model and a field f : Point → Parameter.",
      "Under the stated hypotheses, existentially quantify over a single function P : Cell → LocalDef001 Parameter. P may depend on all the preceding data.",
      "For this same P, quantify universally over cells in the first conclusion, over cells and alternative fields in the second, and over cells and parameter values in the third; existentially quantify over two cells in the fourth."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "Bundled grid conditions: Cell is nonempty; each R(c) is measurable; R(c₁) ∩ R(c₂) is empty whenever c₁ ≠ c₂; and x ∈ Ω if and only if there exists c with x ∈ R(c).",
      "Write A(m, μ, c, f) for the averaging-rule operation. Its bundled locality law states that for every model m′, measure ν, cell c, and fields g and h, pointwise equality of g and h on R(c) implies A(m′, ν, c, g) = A(m′, ν, c, h).",
      "Its bundled constant-preservation law states that for every model m′, measure ν, cell c, and p ∈ Parameter, if ν(R(c)) ≠ 0 and ν(R(c)) ≠ ∞, then A(m′, ν, c, x ↦ p) = p.",
      "For every c ∈ Cell, μ(R(c)) ≠ 0.",
      "For every c ∈ Cell, μ(R(c)) ≠ ∞.",
      "There exist c₁ and c₂ in Cell such that A(m, μ, c₁, f) ≠ A(m, μ, c₂, f)."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "There exists P : Cell → LocalDef001 Parameter satisfying all four following properties simultaneously.",
      "For every cell c, P(c).averagedParameter = A(m, μ, c, f).",
      "For every cell c and every alternative field g : Point → Parameter, if f(x) = g(x) for every x ∈ R(c), then P(c).averagedParameter = A(m, μ, c, g).",
      "For every cell c and every p ∈ Parameter, A(m, μ, c, x ↦ p) = p.",
      "There exist cells d₁ and d₂ such that P(d₁) ≠ P(d₂). These witnesses are not explicitly required to be the witnesses from the unequal-average hypothesis."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "LocalDef001 Parameter is a single-Parameter record; averagedParameter extracts that value.",
      "The grid is a nonempty indexed measurable partition of its stored domain, with exact pairwise disjointness. Its index type need not be finite or countable.",
      "The averaging operation is an abstract Parameter-valued function equipped with locality and conditional constant-preservation laws.",
      "Set.EqOn f g R(c) means exact pointwise agreement of the fields on R(c).",
      "Measures take values in the extended nonnegative reals. The two cell-measure hypotheses together mean 0 < μ(R(c)) < ∞ for every cell."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For any measurable point space, any grid consisting of a nonempty family of pairwise disjoint measurable regions covering its stored domain, any measure, any abstract averaging rule satisfying pointwise locality and preservation of constant fields on regions of positive finite measure, any model, and any parameter field, suppose every cell has positive finite measure and two cells have unequal averages of that field. Then there is an assignment of one-parameter property records to all cells such that each assigned parameter equals that cell's average of the given field, and also equals its average of any alternative field agreeing with the given field throughout that cell. The rule preserves every globally constant parameter field on every cell for the chosen model and measure, and two cells have unequal assigned property records."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "Parameter and Model are arbitrary types. No algebraic, topological, metric, measurable, or physical structure is imposed on them.",
    "No integral formula, arithmetic averaging, linearity, positivity of parameter values, continuity, conservation law, or invariance under changing the measure or model is encoded for A.",
    "The parameter fields are arbitrary total functions on Point. They are not required to be measurable or integrable.",
    "Locality concerns exact pointwise agreement on a cell region. Invariance under changes on measure-zero subsets is not encoded.",
    "Distinct cell regions are exactly disjoint, including their boundary points if any; disjointness only up to null sets is insufficient.",
    "Every cell must have positive finite measure. Empty or zero-measure cells and infinite-measure cells are excluded. The total measure of the domain need not be finite.",
    "The grid's domain need not be all of Point, and no geometric shape, dimension, mesh size, finiteness, or countability condition is imposed.",
    "The unequal-average hypothesis is essential to the stated nonuniformity: the proposition assumes two unequal cell averages rather than deriving them from a weaker claim that the input field varies.",
    "The unequal-average hypothesis forces at least two distinct cells and at least two distinct Parameter values. If all cell averages coincide, including when Cell has only one element or Parameter has at most one element, the implication is vacuous.",
    "Positive cell measure together with the grid's nonempty index type forces nonempty cell regions and hence a nonempty point space and domain in any instance satisfying the hypotheses.",
    "Quantification over a grid and an averaging-rule structure is conditional on those structures existing. The proposition does not assert their existence for arbitrary choices of the underlying types and regions.",
    "The existential assignment is chosen before the universally quantified alternative fields, so a single assignment works for all such fields and all cells.",
    "Constant preservation is asserted for the averaging operation on globally constant fields; it does not assert that the already assigned records equal every constant parameter.",
    "The conclusion specifies no additional properties beyond the one stored parameter, and does not explicitly assert uniqueness of the assignment."
  ],
  "ambiguities": []
}
